record.paper_title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: A strictly non-Volterra QSO is one with P_{ij,k} = 0 whenever k is one of the two parent types i or j. In dimension m = 3, every strictly non-Volterra operator of the displayed six-parameter form has a unique fixed point, that fixed point is not attractive, and 2-cycles and 3-cycles may occur depending on the parameters. Do these conclusions remain true for strictly non-Volterra quadratic stochastic operators in dimensions m >= 4?

evidence.quote: Theorem 6. [40] 1) For any values of parameters a, b, c, d, α, β with (15) the operator (14) has a unique fixed point. Moreover the fixed point is not attractive. 2) The QSO (14) has 2-cycles and 3-cycles depending on the parameters (15).
Problem 11. Is Theorem 6 true for m ≥ 4?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^{m-1}=\{x=(x_1,\dots,x_m)\in\mathbb{R}^m: x_i\ge 0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m x_i=1\}$ be the standard $(m-1)$-simplex. A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) is a map $V:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ defined by
$$ (Vx)_k = \sum_{i,j=1}^m P_{ij,k}\, x_i x_j,\qquad k=1,\dots,m, $$
where the coefficients $P_{ij,k}$ satisfy $P_{ij,k}=P_{ji,k}\ge 0$ and $\sum_{k=1}^m P_{ij,k}=1$ for all $i,j$. The operator $V$ is called strictly non-Volterra if
$$ P_{ij,k}=0\quad\text{whenever } k\in\{i,j\}, $$
i.e. offspring of type $k$ can only be produced by parents whose types are both different from $k$.

A fixed point $x^*\in S^{m-1}$ of $V$ is called attractive if there exists a neighbourhood $U$ of $x^*$ in $S^{m-1}$ such that $V^n(x)\to x^*$ for every $x\in U$. A point $x\in S^{m-1}$ is called a $p$-cycle (periodic point of period $p$) if $V^p(x)=x$ and $V^q(x)\ne x$ for $1\le q<p$.

It is known that for $m=3$ every strictly non-Volterra QSO has a unique fixed point in $S^2$, this fixed point is not attractive, and depending on parameters such operators may admit $2$-cycles and $3$-cycles.

Question: For every $m\ge 4$, is it true that every strictly non-Volterra quadratic stochastic operator on $S^{m-1}$ has a unique fixed point, that this fixed point is never attractive, and that $2$-cycles and $3$-cycles can occur for suitable choices of parameters?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches reveal active research on strictly non-Volterra QSOs in higher-dimensional simplices, including studies of equiprobable cases and specific subclasses, but no source confirms a full proof or disproof of the three claims (unique fixed point, non-attractiveness, existence of 2- and 3-cycles) for all strictly non-Volterra QSOs on $S^{m-1}$ with $m\ge 4$. The status appears to remain unresolved in general.

status_evidence.title: On the Equiprobable Strictly Non-Volterra Quadratic Stochastic Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Equiprobable strictly non-Volterra QSOs have a unique attracting fixed point; only a special subclass is treated.
status_evidence.claim: Only the equiprobable subclass is fully analyzed in higher dimensions, not the general parameter family.

status_evidence.title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators and Processes: Results and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems including extension of the m=3 strictly non-Volterra results to m≥4.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is recorded as open in a survey of QSO problems.
